title: Veterinary Anatomy
subject: 1st Year
description: Veterinary Anatomy focuses on relating structure to function across domestic animal species. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Use labelled diagrams to compare the same structure between species, then explain its functional significance.

title: Veterinary Physiology
subject: 1st Year
description: Veterinary Physiology focuses on understanding how healthy animals maintain normal body functions. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Draw a process from stimulus to response before learning the individual hormones, transporters or feedback loops.

title: Livestock Production Management
subject: 1st Year
description: Livestock Production Management focuses on connecting animal husbandry principles with practical farm management. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare management requirements by species, age and production stage, with welfare and daily observation in view.

title: Veterinary Biochemistry
subject: 2nd Year
description: Veterinary Biochemistry focuses on linking molecular processes with animal health and nutrition. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Build pathway maps around inputs, outputs and regulation instead of memorising disconnected reaction names.

title: Veterinary Microbiology
subject: 2nd Year
description: Veterinary Microbiology focuses on distinguishing infectious agents and the host responses they provoke. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare each agent by classification, transmission and laboratory identification while keeping species context clear.

title: Veterinary Pathology
subject: 2nd Year
description: Veterinary Pathology focuses on recognising mechanisms of disease and the lesions they produce. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Link the underlying mechanism to gross and microscopic changes, then practise describing lesions precisely.

title: Animal Genetics and Breeding
subject: 2nd Year
description: Animal Genetics and Breeding focuses on applying inheritance and population principles to animal improvement. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Work through inheritance and selection examples step by step, checking assumptions before interpreting the result.

title: Animal Nutrition
subject: 2nd Year
description: Animal Nutrition focuses on understanding feeds, nutrient requirements and feeding systems. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare nutrient requirements with feed characteristics and production stage before attempting a balanced ration.

title: Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology
subject: 3rd Year
description: Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology focuses on connecting drug action with species, safety and clinical context. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Organise drug classes by mechanism, indications and adverse effects; verify clinical details against a current professional reference.

title: Veterinary Parasitology
subject: 3rd Year
description: Veterinary Parasitology focuses on understanding parasite life cycles and their significance in animal health. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Sketch life cycles with hosts and infective stages, then connect those stages to diagnosis and prevention.

title: Veterinary Public Health and Epidemiology
subject: 3rd Year
description: Veterinary Public Health and Epidemiology focuses on connecting animal health, human health and population evidence. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Separate individual clinical findings from population measures, and state the denominator whenever interpreting disease frequency.

title: Livestock Products Technology
subject: 3rd Year

This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Use process flow diagrams to connect preservation methods, product quality and the purpose of each processing step.

title: Veterinary and Animal Husbandry Extension Education
subject: 3rd Year

This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Match the communication method to the audience and explain how you would assess whether the advice was understood.

title: Veterinary Clinical Practices I
subject: 3rd Year

subject: 3rd Year

Keep brief observation notes that connect daily routines with animal welfare, production and the reasons behind management decisions.

title: Veterinary Gynaecology and Obstetrics
subject: 4th Year
